provenance_note: Expected design flows, pipe sizes of every segment, the worst branch and its pressure reserve, the booster flag and head and the number of upsizing steps were computed by bench-src/ref/gen_plbsupply.py, an independent Python implementation written from the published method (_plb/sup/METHOD.md plbsupply-1.3: DIN 1988-300 design flows, peak-flow constants and velocity limits, EN 806-3 loading units with the Annex B Fig. B.1 lines (digitised from the licensed copy; since engine plbsupply-1.4), Kell density, IAPWS 2008 viscosity, Colebrook-White solved by Newton iteration, the stated tree and sizing rules), not from the page code. Revision 1.3 (r4) adds the cold and hot systems downstream of the heater tee in the cold + hot mode (Y2-1), the DIN 1988-300 utilisation-unit floor (two largest draw-offs, Y2-2) and the unsized-segment flag no_size_v (Y2-4); their cases are y21-*, y22-*, y24-*. Three invalid-input cases (bad-*: fractional fixture count, units, floor) check that the engine refuses them with the METHOD error codes and the page shows no result. Honest scope: this is consistency with METHOD plus 6 external anchors (cases anchor-*) computed by hand from the DIN 1988-300 peak-flow formula and velocity limits with EN 1057 / EN 12201 bores, one of them (anchor-unit-two-largest) from the DIN utilisation-unit example quoted by SHK Profi 8/2012 (secondary source), one (anchor-flats-en806-fig) from the EN 806-3 Fig. B.1 lines by hand; no DIN 1988-300 Beiblatt or EN 806-3 annex worked example was available to the authors. Case inputs are defined in the generator.
